change.summary: Online merchants selling to EU customers must provide a clearly visible electronic withdrawal function by June 19, 2026, allowing customers to cancel purchases within the cooling-off period. The directive applies to any business selling goods, services, or digital content to EU consumers.

obligations.text: Provide a clearly visible electronic withdrawal function on your store.
obligations.quote: you need to provide a clearly visible electronic withdrawal function, such as a button or link, that customers can use to exercise their withdrawal right directly from your store.

obligations.text: Enable two-step confirmation when a customer exercises the withdrawal right.
obligations.quote: After a customer clicks a withdrawal button or link, they confirm the withdrawal and provide their name and the details of the contract or order they're canceling.

obligations.text: Send automatic withdrawal confirmation to the customer on a durable medium.
obligations.quote: Your store needs to send a confirmation of the withdrawal request to the customer on a durable medium, such as email.

reasons: Your shop is established in Germany and ships to ten EU countries, so you sell to EU consumers.
You sell physical goods — furniture, wooden goods, and leather goods — which fall under the directive's scope of goods sold to EU consumers.
The directive requires any business selling goods to EU consumers to provide an electronic withdrawal function by June 19, 2026.
